title: C192 — Test connector
introduction:
I read this test-connector reference like an address book: the drawing locates a cavity, and its matching table row identifies the circuit and function. Start with the connector identity table, use the housing outline to navigate the drawing, then read the relevant pin-assignment row across. The network name and its high or low designation belong together; neither label is a test result.

This page supports reference reading, not physical access, probing, diagnosis or replacement. The physical viewing side, test conditions and pass/fail values are unspecified. The gauge convention and the meanings of Box, Cols, Size and Used are also undefined here; keep those fields as printed without assigning them extra meaning.

edits.why: I use the broad left-hand projection and the hooked outline at the lower right as landmarks within the drawing. A printed cavity label connects that position to the Cavity column below. These landmarks describe the illustration as displayed; they do not establish whether a physical connector should be viewed from its terminal side or wire side.

Cavity identifies a position in the drawing; Circuit Number identifies the electrical circuit. Read across the matching row to retain its wire Color, Gauge, complete Function and Terminal Part Number. The functions distinguish separate network pairs, so a shared high or low label alone is not enough to identify a circuit. This map establishes those associations without judging whether communication is healthy.

The parts table connects the kit entry with its Service Part and Engineering Shell fields. I keep that cross-reference separate from the pin-assignment table: the pigtail Gauge describes the listed service item and must not replace the circuit-row Gauge. The Image entry is a filename reference, not an additional repair illustration or an installation instruction.
